# Welcome {.unnumbered}

Welcome to **Animal Models: A Graduate Introduction to Mixed Model Equations in Breeding and Genetics**.

## About This Book

This book provides a hands-on, example-driven introduction to mixed model equations for graduate students in animal breeding and genetics. Each chapter starts with small datasets (5-10 animals), demonstrates hand calculations step-by-step, and then scales up to realistic applications using R.

## Learning Approach

Our pedagogical philosophy emphasizes:

- **Start Small**: Every model begins with a toy dataset you can solve by hand to build intuition
- **Show Your Work**: Step-by-step derivations with every symbol defined and dimensions clearly stated
- **Code Included**: R implementations are provided (hidden by default, click "Show code" to reveal)
- **Practice Exercises**: Callouts throughout with extensions and practice problems

## What You'll Learn

By working through this book, you will:

- Understand the theory and practice of mixed model equations (MME)
- Master pedigree-based relationship matrices and their inverses
- Implement animal models for single and multiple traits
- Model longitudinal data with random regressions and reaction norms
- Apply genomic prediction methods (GBLUP, ssGBLUP, Bayesian alphabet)
- Estimate variance components using ANOVA, REML, AI-REML, and Bayesian methods
- Handle categorical traits with threshold models
- Optimize computations for large-scale genetic evaluations

## Prerequisites

Students using this book should have:

- Basic linear algebra (matrix multiplication, inversion, eigenvalues)
- Elementary statistics (linear regression, variance components, distributions)
- R programming experience (helpful but not strictly required - all code is explained)

## Book Structure

The book is organized into six parts:

- **Part I (Chapters 1-3)**: Foundations - introduction, MME basics, and relationship matrices
- **Part II (Chapters 4-7)**: Core animal models - sire model, animal model, repeatability, maternal effects
- **Part III (Chapters 8-11)**: Multi-trait and longitudinal models - correlated traits, test-day, random regression, reaction norms
- **Part IV (Chapters 12-13)**: Categorical traits - threshold models and survival analysis
- **Part V (Chapters 14-17)**: Genomic prediction - G matrix, GBLUP, ssGBLUP, Bayesian methods
- **Part VI (Chapters 18-20)**: Variance estimation and computing - REML, AI-REML, Bayesian, model comparison, computational strategies

Six appendices provide reference material on notation, matrix operations, R code, BLUPF90, datasets, and solutions to practice exercises.

## How to Navigate

Chapters 1-3 form the essential foundation and should be read first. After that, you can follow different paths depending on your interests:

- **Linear path** (comprehensive): Read chapters sequentially
- **Genomics-focused**: Ch 1-3, 5, 8, 14-17, 18, 20
- **Longitudinal models**: Ch 1-3, 5-6, 9-11, 19

See Chapter 1 for a detailed dependency graph showing prerequisites for each chapter.

## Using This Book

All code chunks are collapsed by default to keep focus on concepts and mathematics. Click the "Show code" button on any chunk to see the R implementation. The "Code" menu in the top-right provides options to show all code at once or download source files.

Datasets referenced in examples are available in the `data/` directory of the [book repository](https://github.com/austinputz/animal-models-book).
